title: HelloShift Review, Pricing & Alternatives (2026)
summary: HelloShift review for 2026: AI on guest calls and chats, staff coordination and housekeeping in one platform, no published pricing, plus alternatives.
body_markdown:
*Written by Punn Kam, ex-Google AI engineer and Y Combinator repeat founder. He is the co-founder of Conduit, an AI agent platform built for hospitality, serving 300+ hospitality brands in 140+ languages. Last updated September 1, 2026.*


HelloShift is a hotel operations platform that combines guest messaging, an AI that handles calls and chats, and staff coordination in one system. It publishes no pricing. Its distinguishing idea is that guest communication and internal operations belong in the same tool, which is a real position and also the thing to pressure-test.


## What is HelloShift?


HelloShift consolidates guest communication, front-desk automation, staff coordination, and housekeeping into a single platform. On the guest side it runs SMS, web chat, and an AI that, in its own description, handles "guest calls and chats, trained on your hotel's specific FAQs and documents", 24/7.


On the staff side it replaces logbooks and spreadsheets with messaging, notes, tasks, checklists, and templates. It positions itself for properties from independent boutiques up to major chains.


That combination is the product. Most tools in this category pick a side: guest-facing agent, or internal operations. HelloShift sells both, and whether that is a strength or a compromise depends on which half you actually need.


## How much does HelloShift cost?


HelloShift does not publish pricing. The site routes to a demo request instead. Any figure elsewhere is an estimate.


Among the tools usually shortlisted next to it, Visito publishes from $99/month, Jurny publishes $19 per unit with a $400 monthly minimum, and Conduit publishes $18 per unit per month for Messaging up to $48 for Full Suite. Akia, Asksuite, Bookboost, Operto, and Hostaway publish nothing.


## What is HelloShift good at?


- **Staff coordination.** The logbook replacement is a genuine pain point at properties still running shift handovers on paper or in a group chat.
- **AI on calls and chats.** It covers the phone, which most messaging-only tools do not.
- **One system for two jobs.** Fewer vendors and one guest record across guest-facing and internal work.
- **Housekeeping.** Room status and task flow sit next to the guest thread rather than in a separate app.


## Where does HelloShift fall short?


- **No published pricing.** The demo request is the only route to a number.
- **PMS integrations are not named publicly.** There is an integrations section, but the specific systems are not listed on the page, so verify yours directly and ask whether it writes back or only reads.
- **No published automation rate, implementation time, or compliance detail.** Ask for those on your own data.
- **Breadth versus depth.** A platform covering guest messaging, voice, staff tasks, and housekeeping is doing four jobs. Test the one you are actually buying it for rather than the demo tour.


## Who should pick something else?


HelloShift fits an independent or small-group hotel where the front desk is the bottleneck and internal coordination is genuinely broken. If both halves are true, few tools cover both.


Three situations argue against it. Short-term rentals living in the Airbnb and VRBO inboxes are a poor match for what is fundamentally a hotel product. A gap in booking conversion, before the reservation exists, belongs to Asksuite's stage rather than this one. And running many properties off one reused configuration means asking exactly how the brand layer works, since HelloShift does not describe portfolio controls publicly.


## What are the best HelloShift alternatives?


Ordered by how much of HelloShift's two-sided scope they cover.

Where we sit, plainly: Conduit and HelloShift overlap on the guest agent and on voice, and Conduit's operations layer is a higher tier ($48 per unit per month for Full Suite) rather than included at entry. Our case over HelloShift is the OTA inbox, PMS write-back across every connected system, and brand-over-property rollout, with automation in a 70-90% band across the platform. HelloShift's case over us is that its staff-coordination and housekeeping story is the core of the product rather than a module.


If you are evaluating across a group rather than one hotel,[how to deploy AI messaging across a hotel portfolio](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/how-to-deploy-ai-messaging-across-a-hotel-portfolio) covers the rollout model, and[best AI messaging tools for hotels](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/best-ai-messaging-tools-for-hotels) covers the wider field.


## FAQ


### Does HelloShift answer phone calls?


Yes. HelloShift says its 24/7 AI handles guest calls and chats, trained on the hotel's own FAQs and documents.


### How much does HelloShift cost?


HelloShift does not publish pricing. The site routes to a demo request, so cost comes from a sales conversation.


### Which PMS does HelloShift integrate with?


The site has an integrations section but does not name the specific systems publicly. Verify your PMS directly, and ask whether the integration writes back to the reservation or only reads it.


### Is HelloShift a guest messaging tool or an operations tool?


Both, and that is the point of the product. It runs guest messaging and an AI for calls and chats alongside staff messaging, tasks, checklists, and housekeeping.


### What is the best HelloShift alternative for a hotel group?


Ask how one configuration reaches many properties. HelloShift does not describe portfolio controls publicly. Conduit and Akia both run voice and text on one agent; Conduit adds a brand layer and a property layer for reuse across a group.
